title: Ephemeral-output sweep and client-resume protocol for disconnected streaming sessions
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Goal:
Roll out a conservative, observable mechanism to reclaim ephemeral generation state when clients disconnect or time out, while enabling safe resume for clients that reconnect shortly after a network blip. This ticket implements: a sweep/tombstone lifecycle for in-progress generations, a short-lived resume token scheme, and an integration layer that reconciles KV-cache ownership and billing attribution when a session is reclaimed.

Background & motivation:
We see two common failure modes in streaming: (1) noisy mobile clients that disconnect and immediately reconnect, causing duplicated work and KV cache fragmentation, and (2) lost clients that never resume, leaving warm generation state occupying memory and blocking autoscaled GPUs. Current heuristics aggressively keep generation state for long time windows, which increases memory pressure and cost. We need a middle ground that recovers resources promptly for abandoned sessions while preserving a near-instant resume path for legitimate reconnects.

Scope & non-goals:
- Implement server-side ephemeral-sweep policy, resume token format, and reconciliation hooks for KV cache entries.
- Add metrics + tracing for lifecycle transitions (ACTIVE -> SUSPENDED -> TOMBSTONED).
- Provide a console dashboard slice for suspended sessions older than X.
- Non-goal: UX changes to SDK retry/backoff logic (that's for SDK team; we will document recommended client behavior).

Design overview:
1) Session leases: when a streaming generation is created we issue a short lease (default 60s) that auto-renews on heartbeats or tokenized ACKs from the client.
2) SUSPENDED state: if heartbeat or progress ACKs stop, mark the generation SUSPENDED and start a grace timer (default 5min). Suspended state preserves memory references but marks the session as reclaimable.
3) Resume token: when a client reconnects within the grace window it can present a signed resume token (issued at start) to reattach to the same generation; token usage increments an attach counter in the audit log.
4) TOMBSTONE sweep: after grace window expires, we tombstone generation artifacts (release outgoing buffers, decrement cache ownership, mark KV entries as orphanable). Tombstoned sessions are soft-deleted for 24h before hard GC to assist forensic/debugging.
5) Ownership reconciliation: a background reconciler scans orphanable KV keys and attempts to merge small fragments or reassign them to a warm-backup pool; this avoids fragmentation spikes on heavy reconnect churn.

Trade-offs considered:
- Short leases reduce wasted memory but increase sensitivity to transient packet loss. We mitigate by using client ACKs and conservative defaults (60s / 5min) and providing explicit guidance to SDKs to send lightweight pings.
- Resume tokens introduce complexity and potential privacy considerations; tokens are short-lived, HMAC-signed, and do not contain user payloads.

Acceptance criteria:
- Server correctly transitions sessions through ACTIVE -> SUSPENDED -> TOMBSTONED states in test harness.
- Reconnect with valid resume token reattaches to in-progress generation without duplicating tokens in the KV cache.
- Tombstoned sessions free >90% of previously held memory within 2 minutes of sweep run in scale tests.
- Metrics emitted: suspended_count, resumed_count, tombstone_count, kv_orphans_reassigned, tombstone_gc_latency.
- End-to-end integration tests covering: immediate reconnect, delayed reconnect (within grace), reconnect after tombstone (should not resume), and forced client abort.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (this ticket): implement lease/heartbeat, suspended state, resume token verification, tombstone marker, basic reconciler and metrics. Add unit tests + integration harness.
- Phase 2: refine KV merge heuristics, expose console view, add canary rollout to small subset of hosted customers.
- Phase 3: add autoscaler signal integration so reclaimed resources can be used by additional workloads quicker.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: resume tokens abused for replay -> mitigated by one-time attach counters and short TTLs.
- Risk: tombstone sweeps causing burst memory churn -> mitigated by rate-limited reclaim and gradual release strategy.
- Risk: latency regressions for active sessions -> all added checks are off the hot path; heartbeats are handled by lightweight path with fast-path bypass.

Links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Ephemeral+Session+Lifecycle (internal)
- PR (initial): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421
- Load test results (prototype): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streams/ephemeral-sweep-proto

Operational notes for rollout:
- Feature flag: streaming.ephemeral-sweep.v1 (default off for existing customers).
- Canary: enable for 5% of new hosted sessions, observe suspended_count/resume_rate for 48h.
- Rollback plan: revert flag; artifacts are tombstoned but soft-delete window retains diagnostics for 24h.
